high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary resources and a range of interests. Large parties appeal to me as social occasions. I like the opportunity to talk to many different people, and I often move between conversations rather than remain with only one companion. A surprise party can please me because so much company has come together.

I enjoy being part of a group around an ordinary activity. When I am doing something I like, I often think of involving others. Shared participation can add to the experience even if nobody is leading, competing or trying anything exciting. I can enjoy simply being another member of the gathering.

When my time is free, I often prefer company to being alone. I may seek someone out for an ordinary meal or an uneventful afternoon. Other people being around can be welcome without a special occasion, and long stretches alone often leave me wanting more social contact.

Ordinary crowds do not usually put me off an event. I can enjoy the bustle of people gathered together and need not move to the quietest corner when a space becomes busy. A crowded gathering can be part of its appeal.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. My confidence, affection, leadership, happiness and appetite for danger can vary independently. I can want company without needing to command attention or feel cheerful all the time.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary resources and a range of interests. Large parties are seldom how I want to spend free time. I generally have little desire to circulate among many guests, and a surprise party can leave me wishing for a smaller occasion or time by myself. Knowing the guests does not necessarily make a large celebration appealing.

I feel little pull toward being part of a group simply for shared participation. When I enjoy an activity, I often keep it individual instead of involving others. I can value what I am doing without wanting a group around it, and an optional club gathering is not usually a strong attraction.

I commonly prefer to be alone and want people to leave me to myself. An open afternoon can feel most welcome when it brings uninterrupted solitude. Even pleasant company may be less attractive than spending the time privately, without any need for conversation or shared activity.

Crowded events tend to put me off. I may avoid their busiest periods or choose somewhere quieter. When a gathering fills up, I often want less social bustle and more space away from the crowd.

These are tendencies with ordinary exceptions. I can still care deeply about people, talk comfortably or hold a firm opinion. My preference for solitude and quiet does not require dislike, fear or sadness.
limitations: Full opposite official content, ordinary exceptions; no representativeness, prevalence or human-plausibility claim.
